reviews.text: Watched very soon after the first. Supportings characters are much more interesting and well acted. Set design and use of extras makes the world feel more alive. I found the main villain to be much less imposing in this entry. Main character takes somewhat more of a backseat as he meets his match. I wanted to find out more about the main character but didn't feel like we got much here.

He’s the best shot in the Carolinas! The real treat in these movies, aside from the pleasure of viewing Mr. Gian Maria Volente, is the sound mixing. Why would you get the same ZZZING! Sound effect from shooting a felt hat in midair as you would when the bullet skips off stone? You wouldn’t, but I love it. I wish my pocket watch chimed like his.

on second thought I don't think cowboys are for me it gets the problem from the first movie and does it ten fold paper thin -plot and its basically wandering the movie we just wondermore and more through out the movie I was so bored for the most half I did like the relationship he had with the kids and the older guy (wish it was better established) but honestly maybe cowboy movies aren't for me I'll give em one more chance with the infamous the good the bad and the ugly though

These old westerns are tough for me. They kind of lean too much in to the glory and honor gained from combat and revenge. The instant deaths from gunshots down play the legitimate suffering that happens when you shoot someone. The lesson being told isn’t applicable to the real world, it may work here and there but in the long run it will eat you alive. The movie is very pretty having a significant budget increase from the first film in the trilogy. Enio Morricone is once again very good at his job. Sergio Leone always seems to know how to frame his characters in order to squeeze out as much emotion from his shots as he can. But as pretty as it is I can’t get behind its message.

Though I like the setting of Western Films and this has the infamous Clint Eastwood, I couldn’t get hooked much by this film as much as I thought I would. It just wasn’t my type of film for some reason. Film 31/100

O filme me prendeu bastante no começo, com umas cenas bem intensas. Tem umas partes que parecem meio enroladas, e dá pra sentir que o diretor quis só jogar umas ideias mais “artísticas” ali, sem muita necessidade. Ainda assim, é agradável de assistir. Depois a história começa a virar uma sequência de traições, uma atrás da outra, e em alguns momentos parece até que vão inventando conflito só pra continuar o enredo. No geral eu gostei. Inclusive achei que a primeira parte do banco já teria força pra encerrar o filme. Mas enfim, é um filme ok, com bons momentos dentro desse clima de tensão e conflito.
Bom, pensei que tinha mais ação e tiro, mas tá dboa Cheio de furo de roteiro, mas como eu gosto de filme antigo, vou passar pano. Esperando para ver os próximos da trilogia, espero que sejam melhores
Weakest of the trilogy, don’t know why this is rated better than the first. Don’t know if it’s because of the version I was watching, but had some really odd and jarring cuts as well.
Was really tired so fell asleep for the middle part, so I need to rewatch it But from what i saw, quite fun! Not as good as the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly though

For a few dollars more had potential to be more interesting than a fistful of dollars, but something about the execution left me wanting for more. For starters, the soundtrack for the most part exceeds the original. The gimmick with the pocketwatch helped to build anticipation during the duels  and also gave the scenes a little more emotional weight to them. In contrast to the usual epic western music, the quiet tune puts us in the shoes of the characters a little. The additional layer of melancholy in the music allows us to reflect on the brutality of these duels, and to see them for what they really are: People killing each other. I also think it was a brilliant idea to introduce another lone cowboy into the mix. Lee Van Cleef is just as effortlessly cool as Clint Eastwood and I was excited to see what kind of rivalry will spawn when two capable bounty hunters set their sights on the same target. We get a little bit of that when they first meet but they pretty much get along for the rest of the film. I just feel like that limited the opportunities for creative interactions they could've had, and took away alot of the intrigue I had from the start of the film. Another thing is I'm just not sure I like the story beats here as much as I like the ones in fistful of dollars. This is just a little messy compared to the straightforward traditional hero's journey in the first one. I also think both the Colonel and Indio's backstories and motivations could've been a little better fleshed out. There are definitely ways of doing that without nessecarily stripping away the mystery of the two characters. This would've made the final duel feel a bit more impactful and given it the sauce it needs to surpass the third act of the first film. I think the thing with Leone is that he has such a brilliant style but sometimes he just gets a little too carried away with it. Enough that there's an abundance of style but not enough substance. I still like these westerns but the problem is I can't love it as much as I want to. Maybe I'll change my mind with the good, the bad and the ugly

It’s a decent movie good music good characters. You can’t deny that the story is well written but something was just lacking definitely it is a movie I will watch again definitely it’s just not as strong as some of Sergio Leone’s other stuff

I just really didn’t engage with this one quite as much as a fistful of dollars for some reason. Definitely some amazing scenes, and Eastwood has insane aura like always but I just couldn’t get into it as much as the previous entry.

Pas aussi iconique que le premier mais il reste cool à regarder. Le film joue beaucoup sur des scènes de tension construites par un montage avec des plans de plus en plus rapprochés des personnages et sur la musique intradiégétique de la montre qui malheureusement, malgré le grandiose des compositions de Ennio Morricone, est accompagnée par de la musique extradiégétique qui gâche la tension de la musique seule. L'histoire m'a moins transporté que le premier. Les décors sont toujours grandioses. Donc voilà un bon western spaghetti.
Classic Eastwood, but the weakest of the 3 in the series. Still required viewing in my opinion. Van Cleef’s introduction is phenomenal, and he’s great with Clint.

I was loving this up until I wasn’t. Leone clearly got an upgraded budget on this one and it shows, the movie looks great and plays a lot more with style in a way that I enjoyed. The movie builds a lot of intrigue and sets a lot of things up in the first half, and I was quite excited to see where it was all going. Unfortunately, the pay off never really comes until the last couple minutes. What proceeds is lots of twisting and turning and undercutting the dramatic tension without much to dig your teeth into.

A lot more ambitious and a lot of the originals charm is lost because of this. The mysterious Clint Eastwood doesn't work as well when he needs to share the stage with another hero who is stealing the spotlight at every moment, to the point where I think the movie would have worked better without him. It goes for something a lot more interesting than "lets just kill a bunch of bad guys" but it's just not well setup to deal with a plot deeper than that.

I think I like this more than fistful of dollars The movie started off really slow for me Both the characters and story weren’t doing much for At that point the movie was being carried by the colonel alone Even though the movie wasn’t super long I definitely felt the length The visuals were great as usual. And the music was even more epic than its predecessor. I’m a sucker for the western aesthetic. None of the characters impacted me really. They were quite bland. Clint Eastwood’s characters whole schtick is that he’s a cool calm collected badass but he couldn’t overcome the Colonel’s aura in this film. Colonel was definitely my favourite character in the film. As I was watching the movie I found myself intrigued by his mysterious origins. At the end of the movie after finding out his motivations I wasn’t blown away by the character but I was still fond of him. The budding partnership between the two bounty hunters was appreciated too. The villain I could care less about. Overall the plot also wasn’t that engaging. The ending was nice. A warm end to the partnership Overall it’s not a movie that I imagine I’ll be thinking about in the future. Onto the final installment of the dollars trilogy!

This movie somehow feels like it is less than the sum of it's parts. Outwardly the budget is improved, Lee Van Cleef is here to chew up the scenery, Volonté is back for another villainous turn and Morricone's score is as sharp as ever and the motifs are now front and center with the addition of the haunting diegetic watch theme. But a series of fun and dark set pieces isn't enough to bring the whole picture together in a cohesive unit. Ultimately the characters are a little more one-dimensional, particularly Eastwood's unnamed man who is more morally grey but just has less to do and is less interesting. It is fun to see Van Cleef's Mortimer get the upper hand a few times but never goes much deeper than fun.

This movie is just about two dudes looking as cool as possible for the entire runtime. And to the movie’s credit, they do look really cool while doing cool stuff. But that’s kinda all that’s going on here (other than the gorgeous soundtrack and solid cinematography). The character and narrative through lines barely exist, and I found myself so much less invested in it than A Fistful of Dollars . The movie is entertaining but does very little beyond that; they should’ve spent a few weeks more writing the script.

While not as strong as A Fistful of Dollars , this film was still enjoyable and had very crisp directing. Leone’s style was unique in what angles he chose and how the characters were framed in the shot. The editing was also fun in this one and often dictated the tone and pacing. It was the script that held this one back. The twist and connections between the characters didn’t feel organic. The banter and witty relationships between these bounty hunters and bandits just didn’t land like they did in Leone’s first film. Still a solid watch though and looking forward to moving through the rest of his filmography.

Yo ya no sé si mis gustos están cambiando o que está pasando pero no entiendo cómo está película puede tener tan buenas valoraciones. Posiblemente fuera la cuna del western y más con un protagonista como Clint que está sobresaliente, pero por lo demás me parece muy del montón. Un anónimo y misterioso forastero llega a un pueblo que se encuentra dividido en dos bandos los Busters y los Rojos, en vez de huir ante el problema decide enemistar a los dos clanes y desencadenar una batalla interminable. Espero que las dos siguientes de la trilogía me convezcan más, no quiero decir que sea mala, pero me ha parecido lenta, un poco incoherente y bastante pobre en algunos aspectos. Lo que más me ha gustado ha sido la música.

Not quite as good as the first, although, the score was great and the writing/directing were noticeably better. I know it was the 1960’s but I wasn’t a fan of seeing the same entire cast as the first but everyone is playing a different character. Ramon/Indio looks EXACTLY like an old Italian version of Dylan O’Brien. I could not stop thinking about that.

Another good Clint Eastwood movie but that’s about where the things I liked end. I’m sure in 1965 this movie was revolutionary but I just don’t see the same value in it 61 years later. Maybe I’ll rewatch it someday and think it’s cinema but that day isn’t soon

I liked this a little more than Fistful of Dollars but in the second half it has some of the same problems and really meanders around at times. As a whole though I found the story and filmmaking somewhat better but not by much. Loved the score.

I didn’t like this one as much as the first of the Dollars trilogy. It was longer and felt like it dragged a bit too much when the original was a lot tighter. However, Lee Van Cleef is really cool and this has some moments, but wasn’t as good as the first

Two bounty hunters walk into the desert, discover they have the same hobby, and decide the logical solution is to compete over who can kill more people. For a Few Dollars More is basically cowboy LinkedIn, except the networking events involve revolvers and the job offers come with corpses. Clint Eastwood’s Man with No Name barely speaks, barely reacts, and somehow manages to have more charisma than everyone in the film combined. Meanwhile, Lee Van Cleef’s Colonel Mortimer arrives looking like he has been personally designed by God to wear a black hat. And then there’s the pocket watch. A tiny musical pocket watch somehow becomes one of the most sinister objects in the entire movie. Every time that melody starts playing, you know somebody’s about to have a really bad afternoon. The best part is the chemistry between Eastwood and Van Cleef. They’re not exactly friends. They’re more like two extremely competent coworkers who have accidentally been assigned the same murder project. And Sergio Leone knows how to stretch a moment until you’re practically holding your breath. The close-ups, the silence, the music, the ridiculous amount of dust — everything feels bigger than life.

So is it a common thing to light someone else’s cigarette by docking it with your lit cigarette? Was it common in the Old West? There’s so much cigarette docking in this movie. Definitely the weakest of the Man With No Name trilogy, but still enough here to have an okay time with. An Ennio Morricone score is always going to elevate a piece, and that’s certainly the case here. Not much else to be said, really.

Aura farmer cowboy has a name!!! - MONCO!!! Or is it? I actually have no idea it might be an alias. Monco made a new friend and they tag team a bunch of bank robbers. A lot and I mean a lot of shootouts. Legit cowboy stand offs every 10 minutes. Im lowkey debating on becoming a cowboy now might be a new niche career pathway / prospect. Many things to consider... Clint Eastwood yet again a Mogger!! I wish I looked like bro - so masc and so aura wow very cool stuff.

I think this style of western is a tough sell for me personally. The composition is fine, though there is a good split diopter shot, the plot seems to just move along and I personally don't find the characters all that interesting. Much of the movies script writing feels, flights of fancy esque, it's like a first draft. And I know this is because it's era, but the sound effects changing on every shot took me out of it. Will say though, that score is fantastic and I know understand a few more things in that one Community episode.

Bounty hunter rivalry gets its genuinely stylish sequel treatment, three men's competing pursuit of hidden fortune unfolding across increasingly tense, beautifully staged standoffs throughout the influential western narrative depicted. Nothing about morality stays uncomplicated by genuine, considerable greed and self interest throughout the runtime. Music does enormous atmospheric work throughout, tension building through score as much as through actual gunplay depicted throughout every confrontation. Silence carries enormous weight between the sparse dialogue exchanges throughout its considerable runtime. This remains genuinely influential, confident genre filmmaking, elevated by style and tension in equal, considerable measure throughout. I can see the appeal clearly even where it didn't fully win me over tonight.

Ya con más presupuesto hay una mejor realización, pero el corazón es el mismo. Amo la idea de usar los mismos actores para distintos personajes pero que son idénticos. Una secuela no secuela. La música un 11.

While not as good as "Fistful of dollars" this pseudo-sequel does stand on its own as a buddy / rivalry western where the characters all try to out aurafarm each other. The villain in this one does have a very nice level of dementedness and he does feel threatening when on stage. The movie could have used with some level of higher stakes, as I never felt like the protagonist, Mongo, was ever in any risk or even close to it.

Westerns are a very hit or miss genre for me. I'm not a huge fan of this one. I just really struggle to stay engaged when fuck all is happening and then something irrelevant starts happening and I stare at the wall next to the TV, zoned out. I always feel a sense of unexplained joy when a kid helps our hero/ anti-hero that they have no obligation to. The acting performances are crude for the most part. This is one of those older films that you could enjoy as much blind as you could with sight. I don't hate it, it's not awful, but very little to write home about compared to the luxuries of modern cinema. It gets a more than fair 7.2/10 rating. That soundtrack though, 😬👌. Nobody muddies my boots without getting slept, Eastwood on smoke and I back it. Also, leave my man's hat alone dick'ead.

C'est quand même toujours un peu la même sauce avec Leone et ses western... D'abord le culte voué à m'aura farming de ses cow boy .  Si on était dans animé, vous voyez ces gars avec les vestes posées sur les épaules sans avoir mis les manches, avec les bras croisés, tirant une mine sombre et filmés en contre plongée (la moitié des persos de One piece) ou ces persos aux skills complètement cheatés  genre Levi dans SNK, ce type de perso à l'écriture facile qui sont du miel à fanboy, et bien ce sont ces même mecs version cow boy dans tout les films de Leone. On a la traditionnelle démonstration de tir au pistolet pour montrer qu'on est fortiche en tirant un truc loin ou minuscule. L'affrontement final avec toujours la même musique et l'alternance de plans sur le regard de chacun.. Le même allumage de clope.. Je ne note pas moins que ça parce ça été réalisé antérieurement à ''il était une fois dans l'Ouest'' et ''le bon, la brute et le truand'' et qu'on va dire qu'il a ensuite quand même augmenté avec ces deux là les échelles et la richesse narrative. Mais je peux quand même pas croire, sans avoir vu les deux western restant de sa filmographie, qu'il soit resté toute sa carrière dans ce style de western spaghetti clichés, sans sortir de cette zone confortable pour lui.

Better than the first in terms of music, cinematography, production design, music and Clint Eastwood, Lee Van Cleef duo and the ending was pretty damn good. But fuck me it drags. Pacing is way slower than the first and it felt like they were just wandering around half the time. Still decent but i definitely liked A Fistful of Dollars more

Compared to a fistful of dollars which was only released a year earlier, it makes it seem a student film. In a year Sergio Leone created a movie with more action, more locations, bigger set pieces, considerably longer and more going on, and with multiple high level characters/ actors. However I don’t find myself liking this anymore than FOD. Where it improves in the action it lacks in the writing, I find myself less emersed in this movie, less tension is built and poor dialogue means it’s hard to understand characters motivations, or even what is going on at some points. By no means a bad film, in fact a good one. Like the first so many western tropes arise from this film , there are so many classic sets and shots that make you feel nostalgic for the genre, and this film is still easy viewing that is highly entertaining even if it isn’t enthralling. I’m not dissapointed by the first two movies in the dollars trilogy as they are both good but I don’t quite understand the hype, but I still got a lot of this movie and am excited to see the conclusion as this movie does every job a sequel should.

This movie is fine, I guess. It's the kind of movie that was very, very famous for decades, but sixty years on, it's now largely lost to time, and a revisit does not reveal something that works quite as well anymore. Given the time in which it was made, this could be way worse; for me, it's just moderately compelling and a bit slow. Now that I'm past 50, though, suddenly I'm seeing how hot Clint Eastwood really was at 35.

(Watched via Blu-ray.) I don't know, maybe Spaghetti-Westerns aren't my thing despite my love for the music. I did find this movie to be good but also it just didn't connect with me. I did enjoy the dynamic between Clint Eastwood and the Colonel bounty hunter. And maybe I'll be skewered for saying this but how many subplots and betrayals do they need in this movie? It started to feel pretty complicated with the double crossings and back handed deals.

niente mi dispiace non è proprio il mio genere inaspettato ritorno di ramon, stavolta un po meno villain che nel primo capitolo, l’ho preferito in per un pugno di dollari figo il secondo straniero mega pistolero

Me pareció mas interesante la anterior pero esta no es mala realmente, Clint se roba todas sus escenas y tiene una presencia escénica inpresionante, aparece y no podes dejar de verlo. Pero a pesar de todo eso, me doy cuenta que no es mi género en absoluto, se desde siempre que el Western me aburre y ahora lo puedo volver a confirmar, no por eso le baja puntos a la peli, pero no puedo conectar ni de onda y me da pena por que esta todo bastante bien y en especial con Clint, que ES el Western.
